change_summary: The PLOS One editors retracted the article. The retraction notice's title names this paper's title. The editors retracted it because it was one of a series of submissions with concerns about peer review integrity and potential manipulation of the publication process, and they say these concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results. The paper's headline result is that its recurrent neural network method performs better than recent approaches to malicious URL detection. The retraction applies to the whole article, including those reported performance results, so the findings cannot be relied on. The author either did not respond or could not be reached.
evaluation: In Section 3, your draft names Dutta [14] as the main evidence for choosing an RNN-LSTM URL detector called LURL, and it states that LURL reached 97.4% accuracy on the Phishtank dataset and 96.8% on the Crawler dataset, higher than both comparison detectors. On the strength of these results the draft chose an LSTM over the other detectors it had considered and decided not to run a separate model-selection study. In Section 4, the draft starts from the LURL settings reported by Dutta [14]: two LSTM layers, hidden size 650, learning rate 1.0 with decay 0.73, and it does not plan to tune these settings before the pilot, so that its results can be read against the published ones. The PLOS One editors retracted the article, and they say their concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results. The accuracy results the draft relies on in Section 3 are among the reported results the retraction calls into question, and the model settings the draft adopts in Section 4 come from that retracted article, so the impact on the draft is high, because both its choice of detector and its starting model settings rest on the retracted paper.
recommendation: The PLOS One editors retracted the article, and they say their concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results. In Section 3, the draft names Dutta [14] as the main evidence for its choice of an RNN-LSTM URL detector called LURL, and on the strength of these results it chose an LSTM and decided not to run a separate model-selection study, while in Section 4 it starts from the LURL settings reported by Dutta [14] and does not plan to tune them before the pilot. Before the pilot, raise the Section 4 settings with your co-authors or supervisor, because changing the wording alone won't fix a planned system built on them. In Section 3, remove or replace the citation to Dutta [14] and its accuracy figures, and re-check the choice of an LSTM, for example by running the model-selection study you had skipped.
